title: Lav Diaz’s Venice Title ‘Let Us Through, Dear Ancestors’ Boarded By Heretic For Sales
full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman , Liz Shackleton August 20, 2026 2:38am Let Us Through, Dear Ancestors Venice Film Festival EXCLUSIVE : Lav Diaz ‘s Venice Film Festival title Let Us Through, Dear Ancestors ( Makikiraan Po ) has been boarded by Greek international sales firm Heretic . The film, about Spain’s colonial subjugation of the Philippines, is one of the Filipino auteur’s shorter features running ‘only’ 2 hours 31 minutes. The film, which is playing Out of Competition on the Lido, charts the brutality of Spanish friar Padre Enciso over the population in the 17th century. The synopsis reads: “Spain forcibly transformed the Philippines through sexual violence, exploitation, and religious conversion. Thousands of natives died building 17th-century churches, whose grand architecture stands as monuments to colonization’s brutality.” Related Stories Acquisitions Lightdox Acquires 'Auber 89' Ahead Of Doc's World Premiere at Venice Film Festival Sidebar Giornate Degli Autori News Venice Drama 'I Matter', About Roma Experience, Gets Sales Deal Pic is produced by Bianca Balbuena (Epicmedia Productions Inc) and Montgomery Blencowe (C’est Lovi Productions), with Bradley Liew, Lovi Poe and Louis Wei as executive producers. Watch on Deadline Festival regular Diaz was in Cannes last year with Magalhães ( Magellan ), starring Gael García Bernal, another meditative historical reimagining about colonial legacy and human endurance. This is the latest collaboration between Filipino outfit Epicmedia and Diaz after movies including A Lullaby To The Sorrowful Mystery (Berlinale Silver Bear winner), Berlin Competition entry Season Of The Devil , Venice drama When The Waves Are Gone and Locarno entry Essential Truths of The Lake . Epicmedia is one of the country’s leading arthouse producers and is a regular at major festivals with credits including Rafael Manuel’s Filipiñana , which played at Sundance and Berlin, Truong Minh Quy’s Viet and Nam and Directors Factory Philippines , which both launched at Cannes, Kenneth Dagatan’s In My Mother’s Skin , which played at Sundance and sold to Amazon, and Lorcan Finnegan’s Nocebo, the first Ireland-UK-Philippines coproduction with Eva Green and Mark Strong. That Thing Called Tadhana is one of the highest grossing independent films in Philippine’s box office history. Ioanna Stais, Head of Sales & Acquisitions for Heretic, commented: “We feel incredibly fortunate to be working with Lav Diaz for the first time, a filmmaker whose singular vision and uncompromising body of work we have admired for many years. To be entrusted with bringing his new film to the international market, alongside the brilliant team at Epicmedia, is a real privilege for Heretic.” Bianca Balbuena of producer Epicmedia said: “We are extremely excited to work with Heretic for the first time, especially on a very special project with Lav Diaz. Their energy is so positive! We admire their auteur-driven slate and how they champion unconventional voices. We hope that this becomes a highly fruitful partnership.” Showcases For New ‘SNL’ Cast Members Just Wrapped: Here’s Who Stood Out L.A. title: Seriesly Berlin Selects 18 International Projects For New-Look Pitching Competition
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Alison Hurbert-Burns & Bruna Papandrea’s Made Up Stories Launch Australian Production House The Set Up Vertical Video Economy Worth $150B, Even Without China – Owl & Co Report Dutch Kids TV Classic ‘De Fabeltjeskrant’ Getting International Revival View All August 20, 2026 2:18am Seriesly Berlin Deadline The Seriesly Berlin Project Pitches has selected 18 international projects from the likes of Star Trek: Discovery writer Ted Sullivan and British author Robert Wilson. Participants will take to the stage at the Seriesly Berlin Conference on September 15-16 at the Fotografiska Berlin in a new-look format that divides the projects in three – with the Writers’ Pitch introducing projects at a very early stage and the Co-Production Pitch showcasing more advanced projects. A new Vertical Drama strand has also been added to the program. Among the seven titles contesting The Co-Pro Pitch is Have You Seen Sabine? (working title), an Australia- Germany title developed by Australian producer Susan Schmidt and Avenue Road Productions about writer Virginia Peters’ seven-year investigation into the 2005 murder of a German backpacker in Australia. Related Stories News Dutch Kids TV Classic 'De Fabeltjeskrant' Getting International Revival Festivals Seriesly Berlin Sets Disney+'s 'City Of Blood' Among 13 Premieres I Am God brings German director Hanna Doose ( Dust On Our Hearts ) together with Mayana Films producers Zorana Mušikić and May Odeh (Cannes Critics’ Week Grand Prize winner A Useful Ghost ). The story seems a spiritual festival on the German-Polish border become an ensemble dramedy about healing and reinvention. Watch on Deadline Journey to the West – a German, Czech and Slovakian co-pro – is from Czech-Vietnamese filmmaker Dužan Duong ( Summer School ) and is based on oral histories of the Vietnamese diaspora in the former Eastern Bloc. A Czech broadcaster is attached for co-development. Portugal’s Small Death in Lisbon comes from British author Robert Wilson, who adapts his own novel. It’s in developed at SPi, the company behind Glória , Netflix’s first Portuguese original series, with that show’s creator, Pedro Lopes, among the writers. Another from Germany, The Fallen (working title) unites writer Janett Lederer with Milk teeth director Sophia Bösch and Oksuperdanke producers Linda Hartogs and Dominik Eder for a story of female friendship in a Catholic home for unmarried pregnant women in 1978. The Man Behind a Mask comes from Latvia, and has Anna Kalniņa and producer Serge Serpuhovs from Baltic Pine Films attached. It was developed through the Midpoint Series Launch and is a Cold War thriller about the career of Latvian surgeon Viktors Kalnbērzs, who performed the Soviet Union’s first gender-affirming surgery in Riga in the early 1970s. Finally, Vamos from Italy is a sports dramedy from Berlinale Talents 2026 participant and American Film Institute alumnus Fabrizio Muscia. It explores the rise of padel through an ageing tennis pro forced into the one sport he despises. The Writers’ Picth will be contested by Ireland’s Black Valley , which pairs Irish actor-writer Michael Patric ( The Quiet Girl ) with U.S. writer-producer Sullivan ( Star Trek: Discovery , Riverdale ) and producer Mairtín de Barra of Tailored Films for the story of an unlikely friendship between a traumatised former Army Ranger and a refugee from Sierra Leone. Two projects explore Germany’s far right: The Verdict ( Das Urteil ), from Ali Hakim, Max König and Sandra Müller, pairs their Hakim + König Film together with East Gate Filmproduction, ndF’s new Halle-based subsidiary. It follows a defence attorney in Chemnitz taking on a case a whole city has already decided about who is guilty. The Baseball Bat Years ( Baseballjägerjahre ) is also out of Germany but comes from Venezuelan screenwriter Jorge Patiño. It depicts far-right and racist violence in Germany’s post-reunification years, and is billed as a “psychological thriller about a closeted man in a neo-Nazi cell who fathers a son through rape [and] draws a line from the neo-Nazi violence of 1992 to online radicalisation in 2022.” Bloody Bay is from the UK and was developed by London-based writer-producer Olga Rozanova ( Hope ) and sees four fifty-somethings, a new baby and one explosive secret trapped aboard a 48-foot boat. Italy’s Doggy Style is a multilingual mockumentary from German director, writer and photographer Marlon Rüberg about eight dog parents, one threatened park and a revolution nobody is qualified to lead, while Good Godmother from Serbia sees Belgrade-based animation creators Nick Strutinski and Kirill Semiletov sends a former Fairy Godmother become a therapist to fairytale characters. Hands Up , out of the U.S., is from Neta Weiner, Samira Saraya and Israeli showrunner Michal Cooper Keren. It’s a Berlin-set musical drama about an Israeli rapper and a Palestinian singer under growing political pressure. Vertical Drama Pitch The new Vertical Drama Pitch will see in competition Serial Eyes alumna Madeleine Féret-Fleury and Cédriane Fossat’s Deep Fake from France, a 30-part romcom thriller about a French-Korean influencer whose #30DatesIn30Days challenge turns sinister when a fake account takes over her identity; and Germany’s Just Do It ( Einfach Ma Machen ) – from Annekathrin Bach, Sophia Hein and Mirko Muhshoff – about an overconfident influencer who goes into local politics across 20 fast-paced 100-second episodes. Also out of Germany is What We See from Berlin-based journalist and former TV news executive producer Kate Mar. The 50-part social thriller follows what happens when the public reaches a verdict on a suspicious death long before investigators do. Finally, Worth to Know – an Argentinian, German and Spanish co-pro – is from Berlin-based Argentinian Elda Broglio and Luz Orlando Brennan. It turns the awkward questions of two new stepsisters 20 years apart in age into 28 four-minute episodes. The juries comprise among others writer Anna Winger ( Unorthodo , director Mattie Do ( The Long Walk ), agent Silke Bacher from Homebase Künstleragentur and producer Fleur Winter ( The Crash ). Through a new partnership with Cine Chromatix, the winning project presented in the Co-Production Pitch Selection will receive an in-kind post-production award worth €25,000 ($30,000) for colour grading services. The pitching programme is organised in partnership with the European Writers Desk and Creative Europe MEDIA Desk. Elsewhere, the SteinbrennerMüller Award will again honour one German-language project from the Co-Production Pitch and the Writers’ Pitch that, in the opinion of the jury, has the greatest potential to be successful with audiences. This will receive a communications concept from Berlin-based PR agency SteinbrennerMüller worth €2,000 each. “With more than 250 submissions, making this year’s selection was anything but easy,” says Dennis Ruh, Festival Director of Seriesly Berlin. “What stood out was how strongly many of the projects engage with the world we are living in right now. Creators are responding to political and social realities, but they are doing so through deeply personal stories. At the same time, there is plenty of humour and optimism in the selection. These are very different stories, but many of them have the potential to resonate far beyond the places they come from.” Showcases For New ‘SNL’ Cast Members Just Wrapped: Here’s Who Stood Out L.A. title: San Sebastián Sets Michaël R. Roskam’s ‘Le Faux Soir’ as Closing Night Film
full_text: Aug 20, 2026 2:16am PT San Sebastián Sets Michaël R. Roskam’s ‘Le Faux Soir’ as Closing Night Film The Belgian-French resistance thriller, sold by Goodfellas, brings the 'Bullhead' director back to San Sebastián 12 years after 'The Drop' By Emiliano de Pablos Plus Icon Emiliano de Pablos Latest Mexico’s Madrefoca Boards ‘Isabel Hernández’ as Zoe Films Builds Festival Momentum (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago San Sebastian Adds Jesse Eisenberg, Fred Cavayé, Amanda Kernell Films to Golden Shell Race 6 days ago Bendita Film Sales Picks Up Toronto Discovery Title ‘The Fortunate Isles’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 weeks ago See All 'Le Faux Soir' Courtesy of Goodfellas “ Le Faux Soir ,” a Belgian-French WWII resistance drama from “Bullhead” director Michaël R. Roskam , has been set as the closing night film of this year’s San Sebastián Film Festival. Playing in the festival’s Official Selection out of competition, the film will have its European premiere at San Sebastián after world premiering at Toronto, where it screens in Special Presentations. It will close the festival after the awards ceremony on Sept. 26 at the Kursaal. Related Stories Oscars Budget, 'Engaging' With AI and Hot Memorabilia: Inside the Academy's Annual All-Members Meeting (EXCLUSIVE) Academy Museum Fall Film Events Include 'Marie Antoinette,' 'The Craft,' 'Pan's Labyrinth' - Film News in Brief “Le Faux Soir” is produced by Belgium’s Frakas Productions and Roskam’s Harbor Men Pictures with France’s Rectangle Productions. Goodfellas handles international sales, while Cinéart will release the film in Benelux. Popular on Variety Set in Nazi-occupied Belgium in 1943, the film follows a group of Resistance fighters after the occupying forces turn national daily Le Soir into a propaganda outlet. With commemorations of the 1918 Armistice banned, they hatch a plan to produce a fake edition of the newspaper, reproducing its paper, nameplate and format but filling its pages with articles mocking the German occupiers. The operation has been described as “the world’s first media hack.” Arieh Worthalter (“The Goldman Case”) leads the ensemble, alongside Mélanie Thierry (“Da 5 Bloods”), Karim Leklou (“Jim’s Story”), Mara Taquin (“Zero Fucks Given”), Bouli Lanners (“The Night of the 12th”), Julien Frison (“The Happening”) and François Damiens (“The Bélier Family”). The closing berth brings Roskam back to San Sebastián 12 years after his U.S. crime drama “The Drop,” starring Tom Hardy, Noomi Rapace and James Gandolfini, which won the Jury Prize for Best Screenplay in 2014. Roskam, who previously worked as a journalist for Dutch-language newspaper De Morgen , broke through internationally with feature debut “Bullhead.” After premiering in Berlin’s Panorama section, the film earned an Academy Award nomination for best foreign-language film and landed Roskam on Variety’s Ten Directors to Watch list. He later directed “Racer and the Jailbird,” starring Matthias Schoenaerts and Adèle Exarchopoulos, which screened out of competition at Venice and was selected as Belgium’s Academy Awards entry. He also helmed the first three episodes of Apple TV+ miniseries “Black Bird.” “Le Faux Soir” returns Roskam to the thriller territory that has marked much of his career. Roskam wrote the screenplay, with Bernard Falaise co-credited on dialogue, loosely adapting Marie Istas’ book Le “faux” Soir, 9 novembre 1943 . The 74th San Sebastián Film Festival runs Sept. 18-26. The show’s production design, overseen by set designer Chloe Lamford, is unlike anything ever seen before at the theatre, which is owned by the Royal Shakespeare Company. As well as excavating two stories down to accommodate stage lifts and scenery pieces measuring up to 20-foot high scenery pieces, the design includes 5,291 oz of rubber crumb chippings to create the textured floor, 1.58 miles of steel (not including the audience seating), and 5,000 individually hand-crafted leaves on the tree (which, for the eagle-eyed, also includes seven hidden faces). title: BFI To Launch Refreshed Film Academy Programme With 12 New Skills Hubs Across The UK
full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac BFI To Launch Refreshed Film Academy Programme With 12 New Skills Hubs Across The UK Naomi Watts Set For Zurich’s Golden Eye Award ‘Club Kid’ Trailer: Jordan Firstman Is A Messy Father In His Buzzy Directorial Debut View All August 20, 2026 2:00am BFI Film Academy Photo by Millie Turner/BFI. EXCLUSIVE: The BFI Film Academy, the UK film body’s flagship skills incubator for young people aged 16-25, is expanding with the launch of 12 new BFI Film Academy Hubs across the UK. The BFI has said the scheme will focus on “local provision and devolving funding across the UK.” The 12 hubs will be led by the following organisations: · BFI Film Academy East of England – delivered by 104 Projects CIC · BFI Film Academy East Midlands – delivered by Broadway Nottingham Related Stories Festivals BFI CEO Ben Roberts Gives Keynote Address At Inaugural UK Film Conference: "The Missing Piece, For Me, Is Having Film Firmly In The Classroom" - Edinburgh Film Festival News Isabel Davis Appointed Director Of The BFI Filmmaking Fund · BFI Film Academy London – delivered by CTVC Watch on Deadline · BFI Film Academy North East – delivered by Tyneside Cinema · BFI Film Academy North West – delivered by HOME Manchester · BFI Film Academy South East – delivered by Screen South · BFI Film Academy South West – delivered by Watershed Bristol · BFI Film Academy West Midlands – delivered by Rural Media Charity · BFI Film Academy Yorkshire and The Humber – delivered by Showroom Cinema (Sheffield Media and Exhibition Centre) · BFI Film Academy Northern Ireland – delivered by Nerve Centre · BFI Film Academy Scotland – delivered by Screen Education Edinburgh · BFI Film Academy Wales – delivered by Screen Alliance Wales This new model will run from 2026-29. The BFI has said each BFI Film Academy Hub will engage with schools, youth clubs, colleges and wider community groups to deliver year-round activity to enable local young people aged 16-25 to gain technical and transferable skills, access careers advice and networking opportunities to support them to pursue a career in the screen and wider creative industries. The Hubs will be responsible for curating and delivering introductory courses designed to provide young people with an overview of the film industry with a focus on below-the-line production roles, screen heritage, exhibition and distribution. Ongoing year-round activity – including networking events and masterclasses – will be open to 16-25-year-olds. Each Hub will also have a dedicated Alumni Manager. The BFI Film Academy has been funded through increased investment from the UK Government and ongoing BFI National Lottery Good Cause funding alongside cash from Northern Ireland Screen, Screen Scotland and the Welsh Government. Zakiya Bale, Head of BFI Film Academy Programmes, said the refreshed BFI Film Academy has been “developed to reflect the needs of an ever-changing and fast-paced screen industry.” “BFI Film Academy Hubs will enable young people from across the UK to explore career pathways and develop the skills most in demand across the sector, whatever their background and wherever they’re from,” Bale said. Ian Murray, Minister of State for DCMS, added: “British film is at its best when it tells relatable stories about real lives, and that means the people making those stories need to reflect the country we live in. These nation-spanning BFI Film Academy Hubs will give underrepresented young people the training and connections they need to build a career in film – wherever they live, whatever their background. “Talent is everywhere, but opportunity is not, and we need to put that right. These hubs will help close that gap and build the diverse, skilled workforce our film industry needs for the future, driven through regional delivery partners who know how to best support their local communities.” Showcases For New ‘SNL’ Cast Members Just Wrapped: Here’s Who Stood Out L.A. title: Toei, Shochiku, Kadokawa Among IP Holders Set for TIFFCOM’s Tokyo Adaptation and Remake Market
full_text: Aug 20, 2026 1:48am PT Toei, Shochiku, Kadokawa Among IP Holders Set for TIFFCOM’s Tokyo Adaptation and Remake Market By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Toei, Shochiku, Kadokawa Among IP Holders Set for TIFFCOM’s Tokyo Adaptation and Remake Market 34 minutes ago India’s Epic Studios, Rusk Media Ink 50-Title Vertical Drama Deal (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago Busan Festival Honors Ahn Sung-ki, Market Names Thailand Country of Honor 4 hours ago See All Kawakami Takashi Eight major Japanese publishers, studios and production companies will pitch intellectual property to international buyers at the second edition of Tokyo IP Market: Adaptation & Remake, running Oct. 28-30 at TIFFCOM 2026 in Tokyo. The platform, known as TIPM, will host one-on-one business meetings and open pitching sessions at the Tokyo Metropolitan Industrial Trade Center Hamamatsucho-Kan. Producers from Hollywood, Europe and Asia will attend, seeking to secure rights to adapt and remake Japanese manga, novels and classic films. Related Stories Academy Museum Fall Film Events Include 'Marie Antoinette,' 'The Craft,' 'Pan's Labyrinth' - Film News in Brief Oscars Budget, 'Engaging' With AI and Hot Memorabilia: Inside the Academy's Annual All-Members Meeting (EXCLUSIVE) This year’s participants are Amuse Creative Studio, Kadokawa, Nihon Bungeisha, Nippon Animation, Shochiku, Shufu to Seikatsu Sha, Square Enix and Toei. The eight-company roster marks an expansion from the six IP holders at last year’s inaugural TIPM edition. Popular on Variety The market traces its origins to the Tokyo Story Market, a dedicated service for screen adaptation rights covering Japanese manga and novels, which launched at TIFFCOM in 2023. At TIFFCOM 2025, it was rebranded as TIPM and broadened to encompass film studios and production companies. The platform moved beyond Japan for the first time this past May, when seven companies presented at the Cannes Film Market under the Japan IP Market banner. Among this year’s participants, Shochiku brings a library running from Yasujiro Ozu classics to contemporary genre fare. “For 131 years, Shochiku has created stories that transcend generations,” the studio said. “We are ready to bring these stories to audiences around the world and create the next global hit together with global filmmakers.” Toei, which has already seen its IP adapted overseas as “Power Rangers” and “Yolo,” will present alongside Nihon Bungeisha, publisher of the horror hit “Gannibal,” and game developer and manga publisher Square Enix, whose titles including “Fullmetal Alchemist,” “Soul Eater” and “Kakegurui” have already generated anime, television and film adaptations. “Another key strength is our dedicated international production team so we welcome discussions on both remake rights licensing and co-production opportunities,” Toei said. TIFFCOM, now in its 23rd edition, runs alongside the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival , which opens Oct. 26. title: ‘You Don’t Belong Here’ Director Florin Şerban Sets Next Feature After Winning Locarno’s Golden Leopard (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Aug 20, 2026 1:38am PT ‘You Don’t Belong Here’ Director Florin Şerban Sets Next Feature After Winning Locarno’s Golden Leopard (EXCLUSIVE) By Christopher Vourlias Plus Icon Christopher Vourlias Latest ‘Mother’ Director Teona Mitevska Preps Sequel to Feminist Satirical Drama ‘God Exists, Her Name Is Petrunya’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago ‘Shame and Money’ Director on Sundance-Winning Drama About a Kosovo Family in Free Fall: ‘It’s a Look Into the Past and a Warning to the Future’ 4 days ago Sarajevo Industry Head on How Building a Talent Pipeline Makes Markets and Festivals More Vital Than Ever 7 days ago See All Courtesy Locarno Film Festival Romanian filmmaker Florin Şerban, whose bleak study of systemic racism and toxic masculinity “You Don’t Belong Here” won the Golden Leopard at the recently wrapped Locarno Film Festival , is prepping his next feature film. Speaking to Variety at the Sarajevo Film Festival , where “You Don’t Belong Here” is playing in the main competition, the director shared details about his next project, “Ela, or the Diary of a Dutiful Daughter From Romania,” for which casting is already underway. Related Stories Oscars Budget, 'Engaging' With AI and Hot Memorabilia: Inside the Academy's Annual All-Members Meeting (EXCLUSIVE) Academy Museum Fall Film Events Include 'Marie Antoinette,' 'The Craft,' 'Pan's Labyrinth' - Film News in Brief Written by Adriana Neagoe, “Ela” is “a story about a girl who needs to go away from a family that is very troubled, bounded by alcoholism and violence. She needs to leave before she repeats the story herself, because her life is going in that direction,” said Şerban. Popular on Variety Inspired by the book “Memoirs of a Dutiful Daughter,” by French existentialist philosopher and writer Simone de Beauvoir, the film follows a young Romanian woman who keeps a TikTok diary “where she documents the way she wants her life to be,” said Şerban, “not the way her life actually is.” The film, which has received support from Romania’s CNC, will be produced by Şerban’s Bucharest-based label Fantascope Films, Scharf Film and Avanpost. Şerban is currently searching for international co-producers. The director arrived in Sarajevo fresh off his Locarno triumph, where alongside the top prize, “You Don’t Belong Here” scooped the festival’s Junior Jury and Europa Cinemas Label awards, as well as a special mention for its young star Teodor Butănescu. “The hardest part is the premiere,” the director said, over coffee at Sarajevo’s historic Hotel Europe. “Every single moment watching the film on the huge screen for the first time, literally, it’s like you’ve aged two years. I got out of the cinema drained. I was on the verge of tears.” “You Don’t Belong Here” tells the story of a respected doctor (Adrian Văncică) at a smalltown hospital who’s raising his teenage son, Ioan (Teodor Butănescu), alone after the death of his wife. Unaware that his son is vandalizing cars by night with a gang of masked vigilantes, his world is shaken when he learns that Ioan is a suspect in the murder of a Roma man. Nearly a decade in the making, the film is a somber exploration of masculinity in Southeast Europe, a study of generational divides and a damning portrait of institutionalized racism against Romania’s Roma community. For Şerban, it’s also a personal story inspired by his own experience as a father, and a dawning recognition that fatherhood — and the role of men in society — is rapidly changing in contemporary Europe. “How do we relate to the reality of the world as men in our forties, in our fifties?” the 51-year-old director asked. “There were several changes in the paradigm of how, in this day and age, men should relate to the ones around them. Because this patriarchal model that still exists in the Balkans, that still exists in Europe, little by little, it’s dying. What do we replace it with?” For Marius, there are no easy answers. Middle-aged, hounded by disappointment, he struggles to understand both his son and the generation he represents, never quite finding a way to articulate his love while holding onto “a reality that is vanishing,” according to the director. “For this character, living in this place, there’s no space for love. There’s no time for love,” said Şerban. “You always had this idea that the man had to prove himself. The man had to be a magnet for success, money, fame. He can fail, but he has to get right back up. He cannot shed a tear. He has to be strong. A hero.” “You Don’t Belong Here” marks a return to international festival prominence for the Romanian New Wave veteran, whose debut feature “If I Want to Whistle, I Whistle” premiered in competition at the Berlin Film Festival in 2010, where it won the Grand Prix. Şerban took a break from the director’s chair following the 2018 release of the romantic drama “Love 2. America,” focusing instead on Școala de Film, a Bucharest-based film school he founded in 2010 and later expanded with the help of Romanian actress Cosmina Stratan (“Beyond the Hills”) and the U.S.-based Spanish filmmaker Antonio Méndez Esparza (“Life and Nothing More”). It was among the school’s ranks that the director discovered Butănescu and more than a dozen other actors in “You Don’t Belong Here.” With the school running smoothly in Bucharest, Şerban said he was finally able to return to directing — not least because he also had a story that needed to be told. “It’s a story that’s very close to me. It’s a story that I feel deeply,” he said. “It’s something that I think about a lot. I think it’s the time to raise these questions.” The Sarajevo Film Festival runs Aug. 14 – 21. title: Jonathan Jackson Shares Touching Tribute to Hayden Panettiere: “She Had Such a Bright Light Within Her”
full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All August 19, 2026 11:35pm 'Nashville' Everett Collection Nashville actors Jonathan Jackson and Clare Bowen paid a touching tributes to their late co-star Hayden Panettiere on social media on Wednesday. In a message on Instagram , Jackson, who played Avery Barkley, the bad boy on-again and-off again love interest of Panettiere’s Juliette Barnes in the ABC country music drama, described his co-star as a “sensitive soul” who was “incredibly funny and witty.” Panettiere, who died Sunday in Greenville, South Carolina at 36 , and Jackson starred in Nashville for six seasons, from October 2010 to March 2016. Jackson described how they both “grew up in the industry” and shared that “silent knowing of how intense the struggles can be.” He went on to write that, “she was an absolute joy to work with. Focused, spontaneous and brilliant. The most important thing between friends and coworkers is trust, and we had this.” Related Stories General News Hayden Panettiere's Neighbor Says She Called 911 Multiple Times to Report Disturbances With Star's Boyfriend News DEA Joins Investigation Into Hayden Panettiere's Death, Sources Say He added that it was “not possible to express the shock and grief that so many of us feel right now.” ‘Nashville’ Everett Collection Panettiere’s other Nashville co-star, Australian actress Clare Bowen also posted a tribute on Instagram . Bowen, who played Scarlett O’Connor in the show, wrote a poem set to images of Bowen and Panettiere together from their time working on Nashville together. In one passage, Bowen writes, “I’ll remember you, cheeky in pretty red soles. You said kind things about strangeness, old boots, an old soul. You warned me our monsters only half hid at best…and then fixed the tear in my favorite dress.” In another couplet, Bowen wrote, “We’ll see you someday in your beautiful wings, where vultures and sinners aren’t worthy to sing. Wove from new gold and celestial breath, this isn’t goodbye, it’s just “have a rest.” Following the news of Panettiere’s death, many of her former co-stars on the various film and TV projects she had worked on shared deeply personal and emotional memories of the actress . Nashville alums Connie Britton and Charles Esten , as well as Solange Knowles ( Bring It On: All or Nothing ), Jack Coleman ( Heroes ), Griff Hurst ( A Breed Apart ), Neve Campbell ( Scream ) and Tim Fywell ( Ice Princess ) have all penned tributes to Panettiere. Jonathan Jackson’s full note on Instagram: “I have no words to express the loss of our beloved Hayden. She had such a bright light within her. She was a sensitive soul. Incredibly funny and witty. Amazingly gifted, with a great sense of empathy and compassion. We both grew up in the industry, although she started even younger than me, but we shared that. A silent knowing of how intense the struggles can be. She was an absolute joy to work with. Focused, spontaneous and brilliant. The most important thing between friends and coworkers is trust, and we had this. Elisa and I both love and cherish her deeply, like our own sister. She holds that place in our hearts. My prayer for her every day we worked together was that she would know how loved she is, and that she would find the peace that she was looking for. It’s not possible to express the shock and grief that so many of us feel right now. Our humble prayers are with her family. May God’s angels carry you to your place of rest and true peace. We love you Hayden. You will always be in our hearts. Always. ” Clare Bowen’s poem, posted on Instagram: “It’s been raining in the treehouse for days…for you…you whispered like you’d found the sun, just in June. But you always were full of surprises and dreams pulling at threads and the lines in between. I’ll remember nights side by side in a nest on the same street by fate, that ridiculous bed. The day you got cross that I didn’t scare then by looking glass light cried for everyone there. Thank you for chasing me that day in the dark. I was shattered and bruised, a hollowed out heart. You’d been there. You listened to the bad…and the worst. Our faces painted with the kisses of a good wolf, a good ghost. I’ll remember you, cheeky in pretty red soles. You said kind things about strangeness, old boots, an old soul. You warned me our monsters only half hid at best…and then fixed the tear in my favorite dress. One, in so many in pain, in plain sight, with the last of yourself you kicked on the lights. We’ll see you someday in your beautiful wings, where vultures and sinners aren’t worthy to sing. Wove from new gold and celestial breath, this isn’t goodbye, it’s just “have a rest.” We’ll switch all the coffees, ride our horses too fast…dance with fireflies…and brothers…sisters…friends…under that beautiful blanket of stars. Fly safe, little butterfly. I miss you. Love, Luna Moth.” THR

Each screening will include a guest visit featuring longtime collaborators, among them directors Lee Jang-ho, Bae Chang-ho and Chung Jiyoung, along with actors Kim Bo-Yeon and Bae Jong-ok. BIFF will also publish an essay collection on Ahn’s career and legacy, co-hosted with the Korean Film Archive. Ahn’s screen career stretched nearly seven decades, from his 1957 debut as a child actor through his later years as a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador and longtime member of the BIFF festival committee. title: Hayden Panettiere’s ‘Heroes’ Dad Jack Coleman Pays Tribute To “Extraordinary Young Woman”
full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Hayden Panettiere’s ‘Heroes’ Dad Jack Coleman Pays Tribute To “Extraordinary Young Woman” ‘Furious’ Actor Steve Way Praises Creator Liz Meriwether For Depicting Disabled Romance In “Beautiful, Healthy Way” Nicola Coughlan On Smaller ‘Bridgerton’ Season 5 Role Amid ‘Only Murders In The Building’ Filming: “I Had Such An Epic Run” View All August 19, 2026 8:12pm Jack Coleman and Hayden Panettiere in 'Heroes' Chris Haston/NBC/Courtesy Everett Collection As Hollywood and fans mourn the death of Hayden Panettiere , her Heroes onscreen dad is recalling the late actress’ talent and heart. Jack Coleman , who starred as Claire’s (Panettiere) father Noah Bennett on the NBC superhero drama, remembered Panettiere as a “prodigious talent” and “extraordinary young woman” in a heartfelt statement after her death at age 36 . “I’m heartbroken. I couldn’t begin to put my thoughts into words until now, and they will be inadequate,” he began on Instagram . “I’ve loved Hayden since day one of the pilot of Heroes , 20 years ago, when she introduced herself by shouting ‘daddy’ and throwing her arms around me. From that day on, she called me daddio. She was Haydini, because she was a magician.” Related Stories Obituaries Hayden Panettiere Dies: “Heroes,’ ‘Nashville’ & ‘Scream’ Star Was 36 News Hayden Panettiere’s ‘Heroes’ Co-Stars Pay Tribute To Actress: Greg Grunberg, Dania Ramirez, Masi Oka & More Coleman continued, “She was a prodigious talent. During an early scene, a tear rolled down her cheek on the same line, take after take. I marveled at her technique. ‘It’s not technique,’ she corrected me. ‘I’m not a trained seal. I feel it and the tears just happen to come at that moment.’ She was 16.” Watch on Deadline The actor took aim at the members of the press who “routinely asked obnoxious questions, mostly some version of ‘when are you going to go off the rails?’ Today, we’d recognize those questions for the misogynistic provocations they were.” View this post on Instagram “She was hunted,” he recalled. “Everywhere she went, there were photographers with 300 millimeter lenses—the kind that can make even the most innocent activity look sinister. Once, when she came to our house, paparazzi hid in the bushes behind our yard and drove onto neighbors’ lawns. They were predatory. No one, especially a teenager, should be targeted that way.” Coleman starred alongside Panettiere for the show’s four-season run from 2006 to 2010, during which she played a high school cheerleader who has regenerative powers. Unbeknownst to Claire, her father Noah works for a secret agency that wants to terminated people with special abilities. “She brought joy to the set and a photographic memory,” Coleman continued. “Everyone was in awe of her ability to bring it every take. A tiny colossus who loved to laugh. We laughed a lot. That shining face, that megawatt smile, that wasn’t just for the camera. That was her. She glowed. “Today I’m filled with sorrow and regret. And anger. But that’s for another time. Right now I want to remember an extraordinary young woman who was blessed and cursed. She was vulnerable. She felt everything. It made her a remarkable actor and susceptible to the heartache and thousand natural shocks that flesh is heir to.” Coleman added, “I love you, Hayden. I’ll miss you. I’m so sorry you suffered. I’ll remember how happy you were on set and on the European press tour; how you championed Tess when she was being bullied; your commitment to animal welfare and the courage to put yourself in harm’s way to protect them. I only wish you had been given that same protection. Good night, sweet girl. And flights of angels sing thee to thy rest.” On Monday, Panettiere’s rep confirmed the actress’ death to Deadline, as police in Greenville, South Carolina initially announced that no foul play was suspected. title: Did Alex Vindman Just Get Burned by the Larry David Curse?
full_text: × Skip to main content By Steven Zeitchik Plus Icon Steven Zeitchik Senior Editor, Technology and Politics View All August 19, 2026 7:02pm Florida Democratic Senate candidate, retired Lt. Col. Alex Vindman, concedes to his opponent, Florida State Rep. Angie Nixon, during a primary election-night watch party, held at the American Legion Post 222 event hall on Aug. 18, 2026, in Oakland Park, Florida. Was Vindman Larry David-ed? Joe Raedle/Getty Images Hey let me ask you a question. If I told you about a political candidate with impeccable patriotic bona fides, a compelling backstory and a deep cash reserve, wouldn’t you think he’d win by a landslide or at least turn out a competitive race? That’s what Alex Vindman and his supporters thought. But they underestimated the Larry David factor. Vindman, a Florida Democrat, seemed a lock to win his Senate primary bid on Tuesday. A retired lieutenant colonel in the Army. A Purple Heart-decorated Iraq veteran. A whistleblower on Donald Trump for the 2019 quid pro quo attempt with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that led to an impeachment trial. Vindman had major name recognition. He raised $16 million ($15 million more than his opponent) and was believed to be a big favorite over said rival, Angie Nixon — a little-known Jacksonville-based member of the Florida House of Representatives. Nixon was a DSA candidate in a state that leans moderate, and then some. No way a million Democrats would give the edge to her. (The pair were battling to take on sitting Senator Ashley Moody, a Republican, to finish out the remaining two years of Marco Rubio’s term.) Yet that’s exactly what unfolded Tuesday. Nixon swamped Vindman by more than 12 points, garnering over 700,000 of the total 1.25 million votes. She pulled off the ultimate chat-and-cut. How could this happen to the retired Army lieutenant colonel and Soviet refugee? What did Vindman do to merit this? Did he not respect wood? I’ll tell you what happened. Larry David happened. Vindman appeared in two episodes of Curb Your Enthusiasm as himself, including the series finale, in which he testifies against Larry in his political bribery case. David even campaigned for the candidate, sending out a fundraising text message earlier this summer (including to people who didn’t live anywhere near Florida). “The man is everything I’m not, which should give you an idea of what a tremendous person he is. Vindman is not a puppet. He loves this country. He loves it so much it’s almost off-putting. I love it too, but come on. Get a life, Vindman!” And David, in addition to schlemieling up everything on the show, has a curse attached to him. A curse that ensures people never get the votes they should. It’s called the Curb curse, and it seeks to explain — because there is no explanation — how David never won a writing or acting Emmy in the entire 12-season, 24-year history of the show. Yes, 120 episodes and he never got a thing. (The show won just two overall, for directing and editing.) A post on Screen Rant after his last strikeout in 2024 said: “ Curb Your Enthusiasm Continues a 24-Year Larry David Curse After The Show’s Ending.” And now that the show is over, it carried over to Vindman. David couldn’t win an Emmy in 2024 and Vindman couldn’t win a primary in 2026. If this was a Curb episode, you could almost imagine Vindman showing up at David’s house. “You cost me the election , Larry.” “What are you talking about? I didn’t cost you the election.” “You cost me the election.” “Get the hell out of here! Cost you the election. Poor Candidate Vindman. Like Al Gore. [Fake crying.] Cost him the election.” And then Vindman would angrily leave, but at the end of the episode happen to be in the Santa Monica restaurant when Larry does something untoward and the camera would pan to him and he’d tip someone off and have his revenge. The curse would be avenged. Of course this may not be a curse so much as, you know, simple irascibility. For the character but also the personality — the real-life David wasn’t one for the glad-handing, even at parties, and it’s not like he kissed the awards ring. He didn’t even show up to the Emmys the last time he was nominated. When you attack Elmo , you don’t get love. That irascibility also may have singed Vindman. Who wants to get a hectoring message from David? Especially asking for money. It’s not cool de la. Sure, if you’re trying to analyze the results of the election, you can talk about the Democrats’ swing to the DSA even in a place like Florida, auguring a new future for the party. Or that many of the moderate Dems in Florida have ditched for the GOP and couldn’t vote in the state’s closed primary. But….eh. It was probably Larry. title: Jack Coleman Remembers ‘Heroes’ Co-Star Hayden Panettiere, Says He‘s “Filled With Sorrow, Regret and Anger” Over Death
full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexy Perez Plus Icon Lexy Perez Senior Digital Editor and Producer View All August 19, 2026 4:09pm Jack Coleman and Hayden Panettiere in ‘Heroes.’ Courtesy Everett Collection Jack Coleman is remembering his Heroes co-star Hayden Panettiere . In a tribute shared on his social media, the actor reflected on working with the actress on the NBC drama series where Colman portrayed Noah Bennet, the father to Panettiere’s Claire. “I’m heartbroken. I couldn’t begin to put my thoughts into words until now, and they will be inadequate. I’ve loved Hayden since day one of the pilot of Heroes , 20 years ago, when she introduced herself by shouting ‘daddy’ and throwing her arms around me. From that day on, she called me daddio. She was Haydini, because she was a magician,“ he wrote. Related Stories News Hayden Panettiere's Ex-Boyfriend and Years-Long Abuser Received a Visit From Police After Her Death Movies Liev Schreiber and 'Ukrainians in Exile' Director Janek Ambros Set for Lakes Noir Film Festival Tribute Coleman went on to describe Panettiere as a “prodigious talent,“ who was just 16 at the time of filming. “During an early scene, a tear rolled down her cheek on the same line, take after take. I marveled at her technique. ‘It’s not technique,‘ she corrected me. ‘I’m not a trained seal. I feel it and the tears just happen to come at that moment.‘ She was 16.“ Given her young age at the time, Colman said she had to endure growing up in the public eye and was “hunted“ by photographers. “By 17 she was #1 on IMDB Pro. She was routinely asked obnoxious questions, mostly some version of ‘when are you going to go off the rails?‘ Today, we’d recognize those questions for the misogynistic provocations they were. She was hunted. Everywhere she went, there were photographers with 300 millimeter lenses—the kind that can make even the most innocent activity look sinister. Once, when she came to our house, paparazzi hid in the bushes behind our yard and drove onto neighbors’ lawns. They were predatory. No one, especially a teenager, should be targeted that way,” he wrote. Despite experiencing the heightened media attention, Coleman says Panettiere “brought joy“ to set and treated everyone with kindness. “She brought joy to the set and a photographic memory. Everyone was in awe of her ability to bring it every take. A tiny colossus who loved to laugh. We laughed a lot. That shining face, that megawatt smile, that wasn’t just for the camera. That was her. She glowed,“ Colman continued. As he‘s still processing the news of Panettiere, who died Sunday at age 36 , Coleman said he‘s “filled with sorrow and regret. And anger. But that’s for another time. Right now I want to remember an extraordinary young woman who was blessed and cursed. She was vulnerable. She felt everything. It made her a remarkable actor and susceptible to the heartache and thousand natural shocks that flesh is heir to.” In his parting words, Coleman expressed his love for the actress and his wish that she had been protected and free of suffering. “I love you, Hayden. I’ll miss you. I’m so sorry you suffered. I’ll remember how happy you were on set and on the European press tour; how you championed Tess when she was being bullied; your commitment to animal welfare and the courage to put yourself in harm’s way to protect them. I only wish you had been given that same protection. Good night, sweet girl. And flights of angels sing thee to thy rest.” Panettiere is survived by her parents and daughter, Kaya, whom she shares with ex Wladimir Klitschko. The Greenville County Coroner’s Office said the cause and manner of her death remain pending further investigation, and that there were no obvious signs of trauma to her body. title: Ariana Grande Granted Expedited Subpoena in Lawsuit Over Leaked Music
full_text: Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All August 19, 2026 4:05pm Ariana Grande attends the 83rd Annual Golden Globe Awards at The Beverly Hilton on January 11, 2026 in Beverly Hills, California. Monica Schipper/Getty Images Logo text Ariana Grande has been granted expedited discovery in the pop star’s lawsuit over hackers stealing her unreleased music and photos, according to court documents filed in Los Angeles on Wednesday. Grande first filed her lawsuit against unnamed John Does in July , alleging that hackers had targeted devices of people in her inner circle to steal unreleased music, photos and other materials, subsequently selling the content online on the “dark web for significant sums of money.” Grande’s team filed a request for expedited third-party deposition subpoenas shorter than the usual required waiting period, noting that her team has “identified certain Internet platforms and third-party entities whose services were used to perpetrate the illegal dissemination and transactions, and which are believed to have information and data that will allow Plaintiff to identify and unmask these unknown Defendants.” The court granted that request, noting that “it makes little sense to wait” given that Grande doesn’t have any specific defendants to serve. “And on the merits of the motion, good cause is shown,” judge Mark H. Epstein ruled on Wednesday. “The 20 day waiting period will never run because plaintiff cannot — even with reasonable diligence — discovery the defendant’s identity without this discovery, and therefore will never be able to serve defendants.” Grande said she’s been the victim of this hacking campaign for years, noting that in 2023, as many as 45 of her unreleased songs leaked online. Among the songs that have leaked are “Fantasize,” “That Bitch Is Mine” and “White Tee.” THR

title: ‘Earle Meets World’ Trailer Goes Inside Alix Earle’s Dramatic, Rumor-Filled Year: “Nothing Is Off Limits”
full_text: Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 19, 2026 3:46pm Netflix's 'Earle Meets World' Courtesy of Netflix Logo text “It’s a family business,” reads the tagline for Alix Earle ‘s upcoming reality show, Earle Meets World. Premiering on Netflix next month, the eight-episode series from Fulwell Entertainment follows the influencer as she navigates life with her blended family. The cast includes Ashtin Earle, TJ Earle, Alisa Earle, Ashley Earle, Izabel Earle, Penelope Earle, Thomas Earle, Todd (Alisa’s boyfriend) and Sally Carden (Alix’s best friend). On Wednesday, Netflix released the full trailer for Earle Meets World , following the teaser and first-look photos unveiled last month . The series promises an unfiltered look at Earle’s life after she rose to fame on TikTok in 2022 for posting “Get Ready With Me” videos while attending the University of Miami. Related Stories Next Big Thing Jonathan Daviss Thinks You Will Be Surprised With His Post-'Outer Banks' Role TV Witney Carson Answers Burning 'DWTS' Questions After Pregnancy Announcement, Chats 'Next Pro' The trailer shows Earle dealing with her breakup from ex-boyfriend and NFL player Braxton Berrios, opening up about how she learned of her mother Alisa’s cancer diagnosis and navigating how the family remains close following her father TJ’s affair. “There’s such a different side of my life that people don’t get to see,” Earle says. And the trailer also hints at an answer to questions about Earle’s fallout with Call Her Daddy host Alex Cooper . “She’s trying to paint it as, I’m just this crazy lunatic who is hating her for no reason. There’s a reason,” Earle says in the trailer. Earle signed with Cooper’s Unwell Network in 2023 and launched the Hot Mess podcast under the company. Her departure from Unwell was announced in 2025, sparking speculation about what happened between the two. Cooper addressed Earle in a TikTok posted in April, challenging her to come out and say what happened. Earle later revealed that she planned to discuss the fallout on Earle Meets World rather than on social media. The trailer also pokes fun at the romance rumors surrounding Earle and seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady. Dancing With the Stars pro Jenna Johnson jokes about the speculation, pretending to call Brady and saying, “Tom? Come over, cutie.” Earle and Brady were seen dancing together, with Earle also seen rubbing his back, at a club in St. Barts on New Year’s Eve. They were later spotted dancing together at a Super Bowl party in February. Earle previously teased the possibility of a reality series in an October interview with The Hollywood Reporter , saying, “It’s something we’re talking about a lot as a family. There’s a lot of fun banter and behind the scenes people haven’t seen yet. I love that I get to share experiences with my family. I think they’re such amazing, fun characters that if we ever did something, it would be amazing.” Here’s the official synopsis for Earle Meets World : “Gen-Z’s ultimate It Girl, Alix Earle, is making the next big jump in her career. Can she balance her burgeoning business empire with being that unfiltered, twenty-something, hot mess that America fell in love with? Now she’s taking her candid chaos from your FYP to TV … and nothing is off limits.” Executive producers include Ben Winston, Paul Loban and Charlie Van Vleet for Fulwell Entertainment, as well as Trish Gold and Ally Gasparian. David Grutman’s DGN Studios is also producing, with Evan Rosenfeld serving as an executive producer. Earle Meets World premieres Sept. 4 on Netflix. All eight episodes, which run approximately 45 minutes each, will be released at once. THR

title: IATSE Local 479 Leadership Suspended Amid Corruption Concerns
full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine ‘Earle Meets World’ Trailer: Alix Earle Teases Even More “Unfiltered” Look At Her Life, Including Alex Cooper Drama, In Netflix Unscripted Series ‘My Life With The Walter Boys’ Quietly Returns To Netflix For Season 3; Shane Gillis Comedy ‘Tires’ Gets A Boost ‘Hidden Heroes: A Descendants Story’ Adds Darren Criss, Sherry Cola, James Monroe Iglehart & More As Iconic Disney Characters View All August 19, 2026 3:45pm IATSE Getty Images IATSE has suspended leadership at a prominent U.S. local amid allegations of corruption. Local 479, which represents more than 7,000 film and television technicians across Georgia and Alabama, has been temporarily placed under the stewardship of several special representatives after President Matthew Loeb “declared an emergency” at the division last month, according to a letter sent to members and obtained by Deadline. “This decision was the result of an investigation in which reliable and credible information was brought to my knowledge that the property and membership rights of the Local were subject to irreparable injury if there was no temporary intervention,” Loeb’s letter to members read. Related Stories News DGA & IATSE Urge Fast Track On Paramount-WBD Merger Standoff For Fears That Prolonged Court Battle Will Hurt Jobs News TV & Film Scribes Aren't Spinning A Tale This Time: Jobs Really Have Plummeted In The Last Decade In elected leadership’s stead, Loeb has appointed IATSE International Trustee Andrew Oyaas, International Representative Jamie Fry, Special Representatives Daniel Mahoney and Kevin Amick as the Local’s temporary trustees. Watch on Deadline The letter cites Article Seven, Section 16 of the union’s constitution, which bestows Loeb with the power to remove local leadership “where reliable and credible information is brought to the knowledge of the International President indicating that a condition exists in an affiliated local union whereby the actions of the officers or members thereof endanger the property rights or interests of this Alliance…” While the exact nature of the allegations are unclear, Deadline understands that there were financial issues that were recently brought to international leadership’s attention and prompted further investigation. Per the note from Loeb, a hearing on the matter was scheduled for July 20, which is typically a forum for elected officers to plead their own case on the matter and present evidence to contradict international leaders’ claims. Details on the hearing, as well as potential next steps, are scarce. IATSE declined to comment on the internal matter but confirmed to Deadline that Local 479 remains under a conservatorship. International leadership is juggling quite a bit of strife recently. In addition to apparent internal turmoil, the union is also contending with the possible outcomes of Paramount’s $110-billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. As the antitrust suits move toward a March trial date, Loeb joined forces with DGA executive director Russ Hollander to encourage a quicker reconciliation between Paramount CEO David Ellison and California Attorney General Rob Bonta (who is leading one of the two lawsuits) — whether in court or not. The ongoing merger saga has begun to divide the Hollywood labor community. While DGA and IATSE have expressed a desire to swiftly end the fight, the WGA is also separately suing to block the merger and appears willing to go the distance to do so. title: ‘Widow’s Bay’ Ups Jeff Hiller To Series Regular For Season 2
full_text: Skip to main content By Antonia Blyth Antonia Blyth Executive Editor, Awardsline @antoniablyth More Stories By Antonia ‘Remarkably Bright Creatures’ Star Sally Field Has An Appreciation For Octopuses & Anger Jason Segel Says ‘Shrinking’ Season 4 Will Move Past Acute Grief: “Like A Rom-Com To Me To Try Again At 45 Years Old” – Contenders TV Nominees Studio Octavia Spencer “Felt It Was Incumbent On Me As A Citizen Of The World” To Make ‘Lost Women Of Alaska’ – Contenders TV Nominees Studio View All August 19, 2026 3:31pm Apple TV EXCLUSIVE: Widow’s Bay fans can look forward to a lot more laughs (and possibly screams) with Jeff Hiller in future, Deadline has learned. Come Season 2, Hiller will make the jump from guest star to series regular on the mega-hit much Emmy-nominated show about a haunted Massachusetts island. Hiller, who is repped by Innovative Artists and Odenkirk Provissero Entertainment, met Widow’s Bay creator Katie Dippold in an improv group some 25 years ago. He recently told Deadline that he’d initially sent in a self-tape without telling his old friend. Then, when he was cast, Dippold had warned him that the only role available was a Town Hall staffer who dies. Later, as her script evolved, she called him and said, “Do you mind if I don’t kill you?” Related Stories News All The Songs In 'Ted Lasso' Season 4 So Far Casting 'Murderbot' Adds Steve Buscemi, Wanda Sykes, Patton Oswalt & Many More To Season 2 Cast In the show, Hiller plays Dale, a Town Hall staffer under Matthew Rhys ‘ Mayor Tom Loftis. And in Season 1, Hiller became particularly celebrated for Dale’s iconic scream: “This place is a death trap! RUN!” Watch on Deadline “I have a shorthand with Katie,” Hiller said, recalling their improv years. “She liked when I would melt down and scream. The whole team would always make me do these dramatic monologues where I would end up screaming and crying on the ground. It was a funny bit. And when I read that, I was like, ‘Oh, she wants this .’” Jeff Hiller as Dale and Kate O’Flynn as Patricia in ‘Widow’s Bay’. Apple TV The Apple TV comedy series has garnered a total 19 Emmy nominations, making it the frontrunner of all the new shows this year. And Hiller is Emmy-nominated this year for his guest role of Larry in another Apple TV show, Pluribus — Vince Gilligan’s drama series about a mind-melding pandemic starring Rhea Seehorn as its virus-immune lead. Hiller also won an Emmy last year for his supporting role of Joel in Somebody, Somewhere. This past weekend, Hiller told Deadline that slipping into improv on Widow’s Bay was “actually very tempting. And I didn’t always succeed. They said, ‘We’ll cut around that.’” But one bit made the final cut, he revealed. “One that I think I’m weirdly proud of that literally no one has said that they liked is when Tom is talking and saying, ‘I don’t think this microphone is on.’ And then I say, ‘I can hear you.’” Dale Dickey as Rosemary and Jeff Hiller as Dale in ‘Widow’s Bay’. Dippold is currently in the Widow’s Bay Season 2 writers’ room and has yet to reveal exact plans, but Rhys said the Season 1 finale is “the ultimate setup, I think, for a Season 2. Massive cliffhanger. I’m just talking personally now. A father who now knows the folklore is true. Therefore, if he suddenly leaves the island, his son will die. He realizes he has the Scooby-Doo mission. It’s like, OK, how do we figure this out? What breaks the curse?” The show also stars Stephen Root as local fisherman Wyck. As for what he’d like to see in Season 2, Root told us, “I would love to know more about the backstory. What made Wyck Wyck? What kind of scenes did he see when he was a kid or a young man to make him to want to be a protector of the island to get him to the point where he couldn’t stand it anymore and he said, ‘No, I’m not sitting back anymore. I’m going to tell this mayor that I don’t respect, that I’m going to come out and I’m going to sound the [warning] siren.’” David Ferino/ Deadline And Kate O’Flynn, who has become another fan favorite as Patricia, said, “Next season, I don’t know, but I would love to play a British ancestor of Patricia or something… I like the idea of wigging up and doing a bit of period drama. Why not?” Widow’s Bay Emmy nominees include lead actor Rhys, supporting actors Root, O’Flynn and Dale Dickey as Rosemary, and guest stars Hamish Linklater as the island’s ancient founder Richard Warren and Betty Gilpin as Warren’s wife Sarah, alongside celebrated co-stars Kevin Carroll as Sheriff Bechir, K Callan as secretary June and Kingston Rumi Southwick as Loftis’ son Evan. FX Emmy nominee Charlie Hunnam ( Monster: The Ed Gein Story , Sons of Anarchy ) is putting the M.C. back together—sort of–for an all-new limited series. FX has ordered Legends , a meta-thriller created, developed and executive produced by Hunnam, who will also star, and Jonathan Groff ( Happy Endings, This Fool ), who will serve as showrunner. Ron Perlman , Katey Sagal , Maggie Siff , Mark Boone Junior , Tommy Flanagan , Kim Coates and Theo Rossi join Hunnam on this new adventure. Additional casting will be announced at a later date. On Legends , when the cast of Sons of Anarchy (who will all play themselves) reunites at a fan convention after more than a decade, the line between life and art blurs as the fractured brotherhood finds itself up against a real-world threat more dangerous than anything they ever faced in their show. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News 'Love Story' Stars On Playing An Iconic Romance: The Fights, The Fashion And The New York Of The '90s - Contenders TV Nominees Studio News 'The Drop: A Snowfall Saga' Trailer Reveals Wanda & Leon Taking On The Music Industry Sons of Anarchy , the biker drama created by Kurt Sutter, ran for 7 seasons on FX, with the series concluding in 2014. Perlman played Clay Morrow, Katey Sagal as Gemma Teller Morrow, Maggie Siff as Tara Knowles, Mark Boone Junior as Bobby Munson, Tommy Flanagan as Chibs, Kim Coates as Tig and Theo Rossi as Juice. The show was a ratings juggernaut for the network, which ordered the spinoff Mayans M.C. in 2018 from Sutter and Elgin James, with Emilio Rivera’s character Marcus Alvarez holding court at the center of the new tale. Sutter had plans for other spinoffs, including the prequel series First Nine , and a sequel series about Hunnam’s character Jax Teller’s sons Abel and Thomas. Sutter is not involved in the project, however, he gave Hunnam his blessing to move forward with the series. In the 12 years since, many of the original cast reconnect for fan conventions on a pretty regular basis, with many maintaining tight relationships. The project has been in development with Hunnam for at least three years at FX, before Groff joined the project more recently. ‘Sons of Anarchy’ FX The greenlight arrives following Hunnam’s rave reviews in the Netflix crime-drama series Monster: The Ed Gein Story , portraying the titular suspected serial killer. For his work, he received his first Emmy nomination for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie. The rest of the cast noted above has gone on to star on major projects across TV and film. Most already had established and successful careers in the industry. “When Charlie brought us this inspired idea, we instantly sparked to his bold and entertaining vision,” said Nick Grad, FX Entertainment President. “Charlie’s talents are on full display as a writer, performer and executive producer, leading the real-life brotherhood on an adventure that is both a love letter to the series and a fun meta twist on what fans think they know.” FX’s Legends is developed and executive produced by Hunnam and Jonathan Groff, with Rob Mac, Nicholas Frenkel and Jackie Cohn also serving as executive producers. The series will be produced by FX Productions and 20th Television and will be available to watch on FX and Hulu. Hunnam is repped by CAA, Brillstein Entertainment, and Sloane Offer Weber & Dern.
